lines.text: Today you choose your sales path and build a follow-up kit that sounds like you, sells honestly and never forgets a customer.
Pick the path closest to your work.
Path A is a shop owner, path B is a sales rep who sells to companies, and path C is a service business such as a coaching centre or travel agency.
Every task today has an example for each path, so use your own products and your own words.
Many sales are lost simply because nobody followed up.
Ask the AI for a short sequence, for example on day 3, day 7 and day 14, each with a new, useful reason to reply.
Give it the real facts, and stop when the customer says no.
Common objections are price, timing, trust and a cheaper competitor.
Ask the AI for calm replies that ask a question, show real value and offer a real option.
Never let it invent discounts, warranties or reviews.
A CRM is simply where a team keeps notes about customers, even a shared sheet.
After a call, paste your rough notes without phone numbers, and ask for need, budget, decision maker, objections, next step and date.
Clear notes mean nobody forgets a promise.
Use only true facts, prices and dates.
No fake urgency, no fake reviews and no pretend discounts.
Message only people who agreed to hear from you, and stop when they ask you to stop.
A shop owner gets the most common objection of all: it is too expensive.
The prompt gives the real facts and asks for one question and a real next step.
The reply is warm and helpful, but it says the other table is engineered wood, and we do not know that.
It also promises a five-year warranty, when ours is one year, so we fix both before sending.
A business sales rep asks for three follow-ups, each with a new and useful reason to reply.
The first offers a sample, and the second offers logo printing, if that is a real service you offer.
The last email politely closes the loop, with no pressure and no fake deadline.
Before you save it, check that every offer in it is something you can really do.
A coaching centre counsellor pastes rough notes from a parent’s call, without the phone number.
In seconds the notes become a clean record with six clear fields.
But one small word was added: free, and the parent never heard that from us.
One extra word in a CRM note can turn into a promise, so we delete it.
Save your best checked replies as quick replies or email templates, with blanks for the details.
Only message people who agreed to hear from you, and always respect a stop.
If a bot ever replies for you, it must say it is a bot and pass hard questions to a person.
A simple sheet sorted by follow-up date works as a CRM for a small team.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
